skill.name: routeros-sniffer
skill.description: Guides RouterOS packet capture, TZSP streaming, and mangle-based mirroring for debugging MikroTik traffic with Wireshark or tshark.
skill.summary: Capture RouterOS traffic and stream TZSP packets for protocol debugging.
skill.author: tikoci

security_audit.summary: Most static hits in SKILL.md are Markdown backticks or documentation links, not executable Ruby shell backticks or path traversal. I confirmed privileged sudo examples and temporary pcap file storage as real risks because they can alter host state or leave sensitive traffic captures. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration instructions were found.

remediation.suggestion: Add explicit consent warnings before sudo package installation or host firewall changes, and prefer manual user execution.
Recommend private per-user directories and deletion steps for pcap files that may contain sensitive payloads.
Clarify that HTTP examples are for isolated labs, and prefer HTTPS or local-only networks for real devices.

content.value_statement: RouterOS packet captures can be hard to collect and decode during network troubleshooting. This skill guides RouterOS sniffer setup, TZSP streaming, and Wireshark or tshark receivers.
actual_capabilities: Explains RouterOS sniffer streaming setup for TZSP receivers.
Shows how to save RouterOS packet captures as pcap or pcapng files.
Describes firewall mangle sniff-tzsp rules for targeted mirroring.
Lists Wireshark, tshark, and tcpdump receiver workflows.
Covers CHR lab networking, QEMU host addressing, and cleanup steps.
limitations: The skill cannot access a router without authorized credentials and network reachability.
Hardware-offloaded bridge traffic and some wireless client traffic may not appear in RouterOS captures.
Packet captures can include sensitive payloads and should not be shared without review.
CHR free licenses have speed limits that can affect high-volume tests.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot RouterOS Flows
use_cases.description: Capture a narrow flow and confirm whether packets reach the expected interface or destination.

use_cases.title: Validate Security Controls
use_cases.description: Mirror selected traffic to Wireshark or tshark and verify firewall behavior during an investigation.

use_cases.title: Build CHR Debug Labs
use_cases.description: Use a RouterOS CHR virtual machine to test packet capture workflows before touching production devices.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Simple Capture
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me capture ICMP traffic on a RouterOS interface and view it in the router console. Ask before changing persistent settings.

prompt_templates.title: Stream Traffic to TZSP
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up TZSP streaming from RouterOS to my workstation for DNS troubleshooting. Include receiver setup, filters, and cleanup steps.

prompt_templates.title: Mirror One Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a mangle sniff-tzsp rule for one client and one destination port. Include validation steps and rollback instructions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a CHR Lab Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a CHR lab workflow that starts a local RouterOS VM, streams TZSP traffic, generates test packets, and records cleanup requirements.

output_examples.input: I need to see whether DNS queries from one client reach the WAN.
output: Suggested path: mirror only the client DNS flow with mangle sniff-tzsp.
Receive the TZSP stream in tshark or Wireshark.
Stop capture and remove the mangle rule after validation.

output_examples.input: My CHR lab does not show packets in Wireshark.
output: Check that RouterOS streams to the QEMU host address.
Confirm the host listens on the TZSP port.
Use a short ping test and then reset sniffer settings.

output_examples.input: I need a pcap from a RouterOS device.
output_examples.output: Plan: capture with a tight filter, store the file in a controlled directory, download it securely, and delete router and host copies.

best_practices: Ask for authorization before changing router sniffer, firewall, or host firewall settings.
Use narrow filters for interfaces, addresses, protocols, and durations.
Delete pcap files and remove mangle rules after debugging.
anti_patterns: Do not capture all traffic when a targeted flow is enough.
Do not run sudo installation or firewall commands without explicit user approval.
Do not store sensitive pcap files in shared temporary directories.

faq.question: Does this skill run captures automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance for RouterOS and host receiver commands. Users or agents must run commands in an authorized environment.

faq.question: Can it decode TZSP packets?
faq.answer: It explains how Wireshark and tshark decode TZSP. The skill itself does not parse packet payloads.

faq.question: Is hardware required?
faq.answer: No. A RouterOS CHR virtual machine can support lab testing, but physical routers are also supported.

faq.question: What tools does it expect on the host?
faq.answer: Wireshark or tshark is recommended. Tcpdump can verify raw UDP arrival but does not decode TZSP.

faq.question: How should sensitive captures be handled?
faq.answer: Use narrow filters, secure storage, and short retention. Remove files from router and host systems after analysis.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is documented for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
